frames.narration: The user types "i", then "p". The search box has to show iphone, iphone 15 and ipad within about 100 ms of each keystroke.

First try: a sorted list of the 40 queries. Binary search finds "ip" in 5 steps, then the scan reads all 10 matches and the entry after them: 16 entries read. It works, but the scan grows with the number of matches.
A plain trie finds the "ip" node in 2 steps, but then visits every node below it: 39 reads for "ip" and 78 for "i". The shortest prefixes, which everyone types, are the most expensive.
Precompute: every trie node stores its top 3 completions. A lookup is the walk plus 3 reads: 5 for "ip", 4 for "i". The price is memory: 250 nodes plus 348 list entries, 598 in all, for 40 queries.
The ranking matters as much as the lookup. By popularity the answer is iphone, iphone 15, ipad. Alphabetical would offer ipad, ipad case, ipad pro and hide the query searched 9,800 times.
Typing "iphone 15 case" is 14 keystrokes. Sending every one makes 14 requests; for 10,000 people typing it, 140,000.

Cache the first 2 characters: the busiest prefixes never reach the index, and 12 of 14 requests still do. Debounce 200 ms on top: the client sends only when the typist pauses, so 3 requests go out (30,000 for 10,000 people).
